item.title: Yamal out of Barcelona’s Champions League trip to Sabah
item.description: Lamine Yamal will not travel with his Barcelona team-mates to take on Sabah in the Champions League due to an ankle problem, the Catalan giants said on Monday. Star forward Yamal is being left at home “as a precaution” due to “discomfort in his right ankle” picked up during Sunday’s exciting 3-2 win over Villarreal. The 19-year-old will be available for Barca’s La Liga fixture against Deportivo La Coruna this coming weekend, Barca confirmed. Hansi Flick’s side currently sit three points ahead of Real Madrid at the top of La Liga and are on course to automatically qualify for the last 16 of the Champions League ahead of Wednesday’s match in Azerbaijan. item.title: 2027: We’re not jittery, opposition not ready – Bwala
item.description: Sekinat Osundiji Presidential spokesman Daniel Bwala has said the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) is not worried about the opposition ahead of the 2027 general election, insisting that its political rivals are not prepared for the contest. Bwala, Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, stated this during an interview on Channels Television, where he dismissed suggestions that the ruling party was apprehensive about the growing activities of opposition parties. He said the APC was confident about its political standing, adding that the opposition was not ready for the election. “I do not think the opposition is ready. Those who understand the political trajectory can see that they are already facing defeat,” Bwala said. His comments followed questions about President Tinubu’s decision to expand his campaign itinerary beyond the initial 12 states, amid reports of attacks on campaign materials and the president’s convoy. Defending the adjustment, Bwala described it as a strategic decision rather than an indication that the APC was worried about its political opponents. “President Tinubu is not scared. It is a matter of strategy. He is a chess player, who studies the moves of his opponents before deciding on his next move,” he said. He, however, acknowledged that the ruling party was working to secure voters’ support, saying it would be wrong to assume that Nigerians had already decided to re-elect the president. “We are not worried, but we are working hard because we respect the will of the people. We cannot take their votes for granted,” Bwala said. On the political situation in the North, Bwala described the region as a major battleground in the 2027 election, noting that the president’s campaign activities there were part of a deliberate strategy. He rejected suggestions that the North was united against Tinubu, arguing that the position of individual political leaders should not be interpreted as the collective position of the region. “There is no unanimous adoption of a candidate by any bloc in Nigeria, not even in the North. The position of one political leader should not be taken as the position of the entire region,” he said. Bwala also argued that the president had made significant efforts in the South-West, which informed his decision to concentrate more campaign activities in other regions. Addressing Peter Obi’s performance in the 2023 presidential election, the presidential spokesman said the Labour Party candidate benefited from religious sentiments surrounding the APC’s Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket. “Politics is about strategy. In 2023, Peter Obi benefited from the reaction of some Christians to the APC’s Muslim-Muslim ticket. That was one of the factors that shaped the election,” Bwala said. He further claimed that Obi had visited 12 major churches during the previous election cycle but had not maintained the same pattern ahead of 2027. Bwala alleged that some churches had declined Obi’s requests

item.title: 2027: Obi’s camp alleges plot to link him with IPOB
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The camp of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has alleged a plot by some political actors to link him with the Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) in a campaign it claims is aimed at weakening his growing support in Northern Nigeria. The Peter Obi Media Office (POMR) raised the alarm on Monday, alleging that individuals within the ruling party and some opposition elements were coordinating a propaganda campaign to portray the former Anambra State governor as sympathetic to Biafran separatism. In a statement signed by its spokesperson, Idris Zekeri, the media office said the alleged campaign was intended to discourage Northern Nigerians, particularly young people, from supporting the Obi-Kwankwaso political movement. It alleged that the campaign could involve sponsored reports in Northern newspapers, interviews on radio stations in the region and coordinated narratives on social media. The media office also cited a claim by a social media personality, Gucci Commando, who allegedly said he had visited IPOB leader, Nnamdi Kanu, in Sokoto and attributed political endorsements in support of Obi to him. However, POMR described the claim as questionable, insisting that allegations of such magnitude required independent verification and should not be presented as established facts. The statement read in part: “The Peter Obi Media Office has expressed grave concern about credible intelligence indicating that certain actors within the ruling party, together with elements of the opposition, have hatched a coordinated anti-Obi propaganda effort aimed at exploiting Nigeria’s delicate ethnic and security divisions. “The alleged purpose of this effort is to falsely link Peter Obi to Biafran separatism and depict him as politically aligned with IPOB leader Nnamdi Kanu, apparently to distance Northern Nigerians, especially young people, from the Obi-Kwankwaso political movement.” The media office maintained that Obi was neither an ethnic nor a religious candidate, describing him as a Nigerian whose political vision and aspirations extended beyond ethnic, religious and regional divisions. It said his political objective was to address the country’s economic, security and governance challenges and build a nation that served the interests of all Nigerians. Zekeri said Obi’s commitment to justice, dialogue, national reconciliation and the rule of law should not be misrepresented as support for separatism. He urged Northern Nigerians not to allow what he described as political propaganda to undermine relationships built around the shared aspiration for a better country. “The Obi-Kwankwaso political engagement is a national initiative, not an ethnic enterprise,” he said. The media office also called on those making allegations linking Obi to separatist activities to provide verifiable evidence rather than rely on insinuations. item.title: 2027: Wabara urges opposition leaders to back consensus candidate
item.description: By Steve Oko, Regional Editor, South-East Former Senate President and Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) Board of Trustees, Senator Adolphus Wabara, has backed moves by opposition parties to present a consensus presidential candidate for the 2027 general elections, urging political leaders to sacrifice personal ambitions in the interest of rescuing Nigeria. Wabara said opposition unity had become imperative in view of the country’s political and economic challenges, insisting that national survival, democratic stability and the welfare of Nigerians should take precedence over individual presidential ambitions. The former Senate President, who spoke exclusively with Vanguard, urged opposition presidential hopefuls to rise above personal interests, ego and political calculations and rally behind a credible candidate capable of challenging the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). He said the moment demanded political courage, compromise and patriotism, warning that failure by opposition leaders to unite could weaken the country’s democratic space and prolong the hardship facing citizens. His position comes amid ongoing consultations among opposition parties, including the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Allied People’s Movement (APM) and Social Democratic Party (SDP), to forge a common front ahead of the 2027 presidential election. The parties are expected to deepen discussions at a proposed opposition summit scheduled for November 30, where the question of a consensus presidential candidate and a broader framework for political collaboration are expected to feature prominently. Wabara argued that the opposition’s strength lay not in the number of presidential candidates contesting against one another but in its ability to unite behind one candidate with the political capacity, national reach and popular support to challenge the APC. He warned that allowing multiple opposition candidates to divide the votes of Nigerians seeking change could give the ruling party an electoral advantage without a meaningful challenge. According to him, the overriding objective should be to rescue Nigeria from the control of a few political interests while millions of citizens grapple with economic hardship, insecurity, unemployment and declining living standards. Describing the country’s situation as a threat to democracy, Wabara called on opposition leaders to demonstrate statesmanship by supporting whoever emerges as the consensus candidate, even if doing so requires them to shelve their presidential ambitions. He said: “Nigeria is currently under captivity by a few cabal who should have no business being in power. Our democracy is at stake, and now is the time for uncommon sacrifices for our national survival. “I want the progressive opposition presidential flag bearers to put Nigeria above their individual interests. Let them present the best among them while others step down and rally support for the consensus

item.title: Troops clear suspected IPOB/ESN camp, neutralise IEDs in Imo
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Nigerian Army, working alongside other security agencies, have cleared additional sections of a suspected Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) and Eastern Security Network (ESN) camp in Imo State, uncovering and neutralising improvised explosive devices (IEDs). The operation, conducted on November 21 around Awomama in Oru East Local Government Area, was part of ongoing security offensives launched on November 16 and 17, according to the Army. The joint operation involved troops of the 34 Artillery Brigade and personnel of the Nigerian Navy, Nigerian Air Force, Nigeria Police Force, Department of State Services (DSS) and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC). Security sources said the joint team advanced into the Tango 2 and Tango 3 sections of the suspected camp at about 6:30 a.m., where they discovered that the locations had been heavily fortified with explosives. With the support of Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) personnel, the troops located and successfully neutralised the improvised explosive devices. The operation also led to the recovery of two battery components suspected to have been used to trigger the explosives. The clearance operation is part of sustained efforts by security agencies to dismantle suspected criminal hideouts and prevent attacks in the area. item.title: PANDEF mourns Bayelsa boat accident victims, urges coastal roads
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF) has mourned victims of the boat accident around Oweikorogha Community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, which reportedly claimed several lives, including youths and children. The socio-political organisation also renewed its call on the Federal Government and governments of oil-producing states to prioritise the construction of roads and bridges to connect isolated coastal communities and reduce their dependence on water transportation. PANDEF, in a statement signed by its National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, said it received the news of the accident, which occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, with shock and sadness. The organisation described the incident as heartbreaking and commiserated with the affected families, the Bayelsa State Government, residents of Southern Ijaw and the affected communities. It said the tragedy reinforced its longstanding position that inadequate road infrastructure had left many coastal communities with limited transportation options, making water travel a necessity for their residents. According to PANDEF, the Federal Government should, as an interim measure, support state governments in acquiring adequate seaworthy vessels to meet the transportation needs of coastal communities. The organisation also called on emergency relief agencies, security agencies and regulatory authorities to work with the Bayelsa State Government to provide assistance to survivors and bereaved families. It urged the relevant authorities to strengthen enforcement of water transportation safety regulations, including compliance with passenger safety protocols, the use of appropriate safety equipment and the operation of vessels that meet prescribed seaworthiness standards. PANDEF said measures must be taken to prevent a recurrence of such tragedies, stressing the need for improved transportation infrastructure and stricter safety standards across the coastal areas. The statement read in part: “While mourning this tragic loss, PANDEF calls on the relevant emergency relief agencies, security agencies and regulatory authorities to work closely with the Bayelsa State Government to ensure that all necessary measures are taken to assuage the impact on survivors and bereaved families. “More importantly, [they should] take all necessary measures to prevent a recurrence of such tragedies.” The organisation expressed solidarity with the victims’ families and the people of Bayelsa State, praying for the repose of the souls of the deceased and comfort for those affected by the tragedy. item.title: Alice Huang had contact with China spy agency during Nvidia boss affair – Report
item.description: Alice Huang, the alleged spy at the center of the Nvidia scandal, was in touch with an official from China’s top spy agency during an affair with the chip giant’s former chief executive Jensen Huang, the New York Times reported on Sunday. Alice Huang was this month outed as a suspected Chinese spy, accused of having an affair with Jensen Huang while digging up company secrets for Beijing. She was in contact with an officer of China’s Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the Times reported, citing people with knowledge of the intelligence. Alice Huang, who is no relation to Jensen, previously led Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based tech group under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese firms gain access to Nvidia chips, possibly in violation of US export controls. According to the Times, Alice Huang’s contacts with the Chinese spy agency correspond to the affair as well as a period when Megaspeed was acquiring large amounts of advanced Nvidia chips. The Times also reported that US intelligence agencies have gathered evidence that Alice Huang’s business partner Kang Wei — who the newspaper said was often introduced as her husband — worked with the same Chinese spy agency. Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia’s chief executive earlier this month, following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang. He is to be questioned by US lawmakers on December 1 over national security concerns. The upheaval has battered shares of Nvidia which is at the center of an AI boom that has helped propel markets to record highs and boosted economic growth around the globe. The post Alice Huang had contact with China spy agency during Nvidia boss affair – Report appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Senegal to know fate of AFCON title appeal Tuesday – CAS
item.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) announced that a verdict on Senegal’s appeal of the decision to strip them of the Africa Cup of Nations title in favour of Morocco will come on Tuesday. CAS’s ruling comes after a hearing of the case, over a chaotic AFCON final in January, which took place behind closed doors at its headquarters in Lausanne on October 8. “The parties have been notified that the CAS decision will be rendered Tuesday 24 November 2026 in the course of the afternoon (GMT),” CAS said in a short statement on Monday. At the January 18 final in Rabat, Senegal won 1-0 thanks to Pape Gueye’s extra-time goal, but the occasion was marred near the end of normal time when many Senegal players walked off the pitch in protest at the decision to award Morocco a penalty with the match still goalless. Some Senegalese supporters also attempted a pitch invasion, and the game was held up for almost 20 minutes before the Senegal players returned. In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) overturned that result, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title. In response, the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) denounced the ruling as the “most blatant administrative robbery in the history of our sport”. The Senegal team even paraded the trophy to their supporters in Paris at the end of March. The post Senegal to know fate of AFCON title appeal Tuesday – CAS appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Fire Destroys Over 100 Shops At Kano Fish Market, Traders Count Losses
item.description: A fire outbreak at Kano Fish Market along Zaria Road has destroyed more than 100 shops, leaving traders counting losses estimated to run into billions of naira. The fire reportedly broke out at about 9:00 p.m. on Sunday, near Kano Line Motor Park, spreading across sections of the market and destroying shops, containers and goods. Reports indicate that approximately 150 shops and 200 containers were affected by the inferno, with some traders reportedly losing goods valued at millions of naira. Traders trying to salvage what is left after the fire One of the affected traders, Usman Sani, recounted how the fire spread through the market, destroying shops and goods before traders could salvage their belongings. “We received the news of the fire and rushed to the market, but by the time we got here, the flames had already spread. Many shops were affected, and traders lost goods worth millions of naira. The situation is heartbreaking,” he said. The huge fire on Sunday, November 22, 2026, as it razes the fish shop in Kano State. Another trader, Musa Inuwa, described the incident as a major setback for those who depend on the market for their livelihood. “Many of us depend entirely on this business to feed our families. We have lost our goods and capital, and we do not know where to start from. We are appealing to the government to come to our assistance,” he said. The affected traders are appealing to the Kano State Government and relevant authorities for urgent intervention to support those who lost their businesses. The Kano State Fire Service reportedly received a distress call at about 9:58 p.m. and deployed personnel to the scene, arriving four minutes later. item.title: UK Digging New Reservoirs To Fight Persistent Droughts
item.description: Britain has long had a reputation for rain. But as it adapts to a warmer, drier climate, the UK is racing to complete a huge new reservoir, its first in over three decades. Bulldozers have been digging up the ground for the vast £800-million ($1 billion) Havant Thicket project near the southern coastal port of Portsmouth. Like much of Europe, Britain endured record-breaking heat this summer and, despite the return of rains as the country moves into winter, parts are still grappling with drought conditions. “We’ve got increasing problems with our water security in the UK,” climate scientist Hannah Cloke from Reading University told AFP. “We need to really think about how we’re storing that water because this problem is only going to get worse.” Scientists have warned extreme weather events are likely to become more frequent and more intense as the global climate changes. Workers carry out construction work at the site of the new Havant Thicket Reservoir in Hampshire, southern England, on November 5, 2026. Photo by CARLOS JASSO / AFP By mid-November, almost all of England remained in drought, with some areas classified as suffering severe drought, according to the Environment Agency. Potentially exacerbating matters, existing reservoirs were only 60 percent full, 19 percentage points below the seasonal average. For policymakers, the situation poses a longer-term challenge as the thirst for water increases with a rising population and the growth of heavy water-using industries such as data centres. Under England’s National Framework for Water Resources published in 2025, the country could face a daily water supply shortfall of five billion litres (1.3 billion gallons) by 2055, with resources under pressure. At the sprawling Havant Thicket site, Portsmouth Water chief executive Bob Taylor said the industry was waking up to the scale of the challenge after successive droughts and hot summers. Workers carry out construction work at the site of the new Havant Thicket Reservoir in Hampshire, southern England, on November 5, 2026. Photo by CARLOS JASSO / AFP The issue, he stressed, was not necessarily how much rain falls over the course of a year, but when it falls. Winters are becoming wetter, while summers are increasingly dry. “Without reservoirs you can’t store that intense rainfall and put it somewhere where it can be used at another time,” Taylor said. The new reservoir will eventually hold up to 8.7 billion litres of water, helping secure supplies for hundreds of thousands of people. Fed in part by winter surpluses from a major spring already tapped by Portsmouth Water, it has become one of the flagship projects in a broader shift in Britain’s water strategy. The government has approved the construction of nine major reservoirs by 2050, and last year relaxed planning rules to speed up projects after decades of under-investment in water infrastructure. Together, the future reservoirs could deliver an additional 670 million litres of water per day. ‘

item.title: Alleged Sexual Assault: Daura Emirate Probes Viral Video As Tourist Accuses Emir of Inappropriate Conduct
item.description: Tension has gripped Daura in Katsina State following the emergence of a viral video in which a foreign female tourist accused the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Dr. Faruk Umar Faruk, of inappropriate sexual conduct during a visit to his palace. The allegations, which have generated widespread reactions on social media, are currently under review by the Daura Emirate Council, which says it is investigating the authenticity of the video and the claims made by the tourist. The woman, identified as Mirka and known on Instagram by the handle @beduinqa, posted the video after completing a 30-day tour of different parts of Nigeria. In a statement accompanying the footage, she alleged that the incident occurred on Saturday, November 14, 2026, when she visited the Emir’s palace in Daura. According to her account, she was ushered into a large room where she met privately with the Emir. She alleged that during their conversation, the Emir held her hand and began playing with it despite her objections. Mirka claimed she repeatedly asked him to stop, writing: “I told him, ‘Your Highness, no, no, no. You should not be touching me like that.’ But he just laughed.” She further alleged that as the meeting ended, the Emir hugged her, kissed her on the cheeks and touched her breast without her consent. The tourist said the encounter left her shocked, disgusted and emotionally distressed, adding that it was the only alleged incident of sexual harassment she experienced throughout her month-long tour of Nigeria. She also claimed she was able to capture the encounter using a pair of Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses equipped with a built-in camera, and alleged that she may not have been the first woman to experience such conduct but might have been the first to record it. Reacting to the development, the spokesman of the Daura Emirate Council, Ibrahim Usman Murtala, confirmed in a telephone interview with our correspondent on Monday that the Emirate was aware of the viral video. Emir of Daura, Alhaji Dr. Faruk Umar Faruk He said the Emirate had commenced a review of the footage to determine its authenticity and ascertain whether it had been altered or manipulated using any form of technology. According to him, the Emirate will issue an official statement after concluding its internal review of the matter. As of the time of filing this report, neither the Emir of Daura nor the Daura Emirate Council had issued a substantive response to the specific allegations made by the tourist. Foreign tourist, Mirka, during her visit to the Emir’s palace in Daura. Meanwhile, residents of Daura described the development as disturbing, saying allegations of such magnitude should be thoroughly investigated to establish the facts while safeguarding the integrity of Nigeria’s traditional institutions and ensuring justice for all parties involved. item.title: Ukraine Claims Strikes On Two Russian Boats Off Libya
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday said Ukraine was behind strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya, adding that one of them sank in the latest spillover from Moscow’s war with Kyiv. The attacks on Sunday near the Libyan port of Benghazi come at a time when Ukraine has stepped up its strikes against Russia far from the frontlines. But the United Nations condemned the strikes, warning against the prospect of a country still divided after the Libyan civil war becoming “a battleground for foreign conflicts”. “It all took place off the coast of Libya. Our warriors deployed seven Ukrainian-made naval drones. Despite all the enemy’s efforts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk,” Zelensky wrote on X. This handout satellite photo taken and released by the Satellite image ©2026 Vantor shows the view of a Russian ship docked at the Benghazi port before a strike, on November 21, 2026. Photo by HANDOUT / SATELLITE IMAGE ©2026 VANTOR / AFP The Ukrainian leader claimed the Merkury was “one of their newest ships, commissioned in 2023, during the full-scale war”. “Our second target was the Russian dry cargo vessel MV ANGARA, which the enemy used to transport weapons. Result: target hit,” he added. A Ka-27 combat helicopter was also destroyed in the strike on the Merkury, Zelensky said. Sunday’s strikes came after a drone hit a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea on Saturday, close to the waters of Finland, whose border guard said the strike was Ukrainian. The UN mission in Libya expressed “serious concern” over the attacks, calling for “an immediate, independent and transparent investigation”. “Libya cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts,” the UNSMIL wrote on X. item.title: India To Give $1.6b Aid Package To Flood-Hit Nepal
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi offered a $1.6 billion “development cooperation” package to neighbouring Nepal on Monday in the wake of devastating Himalayan floods. “We express our deep condolences for the loss of lives caused by the devastating floods in Nepal in August,” Modi said, standing alongside his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah in New Delhi. “To support Nepal’s reconstruction, and give fresh momentum to its long-term development, we announce a development cooperation package worth 240 billion Nepali rupees ($1.6 billion),” he said. India did not immediately give specific details of what the development package included. Shah was given a military honour guard parade at the presidential palace in New Delhi, on his first trip to a neighbouring country since taking office in March. Rescuers use an excavator to transport a flood survivor following flash floods and a landslide at Devighat in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on August 26, 2026. Photo by PRAKASH MATHEMA / AFP The rapper-turned-politician came to power following a wave of youth-led anti-corruption protests in September 2025. Shah, 36, wearing his trademark sunglasses and dressed in black, was given a bear hug by Modi, 76, dressed all in white. Unlike his predecessors, Shah had initially refrained from foreign visits since becoming prime minister. His first overseas trip was to New York in September, where he addressed the United Nations General Assembly as Nepal reeled from a deadly tsunami-like flood, triggered by a high-altitude glacial mountain collapse, that killed more than 1,400 people and left 5,000 missing. ‘Deal with future disasters’ A man looks at the remains in the aftermath of flash floods at Trishuli in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on September 7, 2026. Photo by PEDRO PARDO / AFP Nepal, a largely rural country that contributes little to global greenhouse gas emissions, estimates reconstruction will cost $4.78 billion. Shah said it showed the “imperative to address the challenges of climate change through collective action”. In October, the United Nations’ climate loss and damage fund agreed the modest sum of $20 million in aid to Nepal — the maximum amount countries can request in a single application — and the first time it has set aside money for any country. Nepal, a landlocked Himalayan nation of 30 million people, has long had to balance its relations with its two giant neighbours, India and China. “Our commitment will be to help affected families rebuild their lives, create new opportunities and further strengthen Nepal’s capacity to deal with future disasters,” Modi said. item.title: Eisenkot, Netanyahu parties to meet again for Israel coalition talks
item.description: The parties of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot, who is tasked with forming the next Israeli government, are due to resume coalition talks on Monday after negotiations a day earlier delivered no agreement. The third round of talks comes as Eisenkot’s wide-ranging camp faces divisions on whether to forge alliances with the ultra-Orthodox parties, or the Arab-majority lists, or whether to form a national unity government with Netanyahu’s Likud. Former military chief Eisenkot has until December 6 — a deadline which can be extended by 14 days — to form a government to replace Netanyahu after the October election failed to deliver a clear majority for either bloc. Delegations from Eisenkot’s centrist Yashar party and Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud are due to meet on Monday evening for a third round of negotiations, a spokesperson for Likud told AFP. Representatives from each party met for nearly four hours on Sunday and laid out their positions “on a range of substantive issues,” with no sign of a breakthrough. – Political ‘boycotts’ – On Saturday, Yashar presented the talks as “a genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government”, saying that Eisenkot had asked his representatives to explore all options. Likud immediately laid down several conditions for its participation in a unity government, including an end to “all personal attacks” and political “boycotts” targeting Netanyahu and his government. Eisenkot’s 48-member bloc needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority and remains divided over how to build a coalition. Short of 61 lawmakers, Eisenkot’s bloc could form a minority government. The head of the left-leaning Democrats party, Yair Golan, on Monday called for an end to the “sham talks with Likud”. Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel. Such an arrangement could allow Netanyahu to keep his political leverage against the corruption charges he faces, as well as continue to oppose the creation of an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023. But that prospect runs up against Eisenkot’s refusal to serve in a cabinet led by Netanyahu, against whom he centred his campaign. Last week, Eisenkot said that he would be prepared to put forward a minority national emergency government for a parliamentary vote should efforts to create a broad-based government fail. item.title: Nigeria not ready to host World Cup – FIFA president
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde FIFA President Gianni Infantino has said Nigeria is not currently ready to host the FIFA World Cup, citing the need for investment in stadiums, hotels, airports and transportation infrastructure. Infantino made this known in an interview with Arise News, aired on Monday, while responding to a question on what it would take for a country like Nigeria to host the global football tournament. “The key for hosting a World Cup is the infrastructure: the stadiums, hotels, airports, and transportation. This is where the investment is really necessary. “A country like Nigeria has the resources, the passion, and the will as well,” he said. Asked directly whether Nigeria was ready to host the World Cup, Infantino replied, “Today, no, but tomorrow, why not?” Nigeria last hosted a FIFA tournament in 2009, when it staged the FIFA U-17 World Cup, with Switzerland defeating Nigeria’s Golden Eaglets 1-0 in the final in Abuja. On his 10-year tenure as FIFA president, Infantino said the organisation’s growth and the expansion of its competitions reflected the work done under his leadership. “I think the facts really speak quite loudly here. Speak for themselves. The organisation of the World Cups, both for men and women, increasing the number of teams, increasing the competitive balance of these competitions, and the revenue news. “Of course, we moved from a bit more than 5 billion before I arrived to 16 billion in this last cycle,” he said. He added that football and FIFA had continued to grow, saying such progress required hard work and strict compliance with established standards. “Football is growing. FIFA is growing. This is not possible if you don’t work hard, but also if you don’t work in compliance with the highest possible standard,” he said. Infantino was in Nigeria over the weekend, where on Friday, he inspected the remodelled Warri City Stadium alongside FIFA Secretary-General Mattias Grafström. During the visit, h e praised Nigeria’s football heritage and the country’s contribution to the global game , noting that some of the world’s finest players came from Nigeria, particularly Delta State. “This stadium is fantastic. It has everything you can dream of. I just would love to wear some shorts and kick the ball. So as soon as it’s completely finished, we’d come and play games with all these great Nigerian legends who come from this region. “Not just in Nigeria, but some of the best players in the world come from Nigeria, come from Delta State,” he said. At the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football in Abuja, on Saturday, Infantino also commended President Bola Tinubu for investments in sports facilities, saying they demonstrated the country’s commitment to its young population. “He is doing, together with all of you, fantastic job here in Nigeria, showing that you are a country projected into the future,” he said. item.title: Nothing will stop 750km Coastal Highway – Umahi
item.description: By John Alechenu, Abuja The Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, has reaffirmed President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to completing the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, declaring that nothing will stop the project. Umahi spoke during an inspection of bridges on Sections 1 and 2 of the highway. The disclosure was made in a statement by Francis Nwaze, Senior Special Assistant to the Minister, in Abuja on Monday. He quoted the minister as saying, “Nothing will happen to the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, which passes through the nine coastal states. The President has directed that the project must be completed as envisaged.” Umahi described the highway as a profitable national investment capable of generating revenue, attracting private investors and unlocking tourism and industrial opportunities. “We are using concrete, and so we are entitled to carbon credits claim. We are also using solar instead of conventional electricity; we are entitled to carbon credits,” he said. He added that the superhighway would accommodate tourism facilities, factories, CCTV surveillance and other commercial infrastructure, with private investors already showing interest in recovering costs through investment arrangements. The minister disclosed that President Tinubu is expected to commission Section 1 this month or early December. He also clarified that the reconstruction of the East-West Road is an additional commitment by the President and does not replace or affect the Coastal Highway. He described the ongoing 1,068-kilometre Sokoto-Badagry Road as another major infrastructure undertaking of the administration, stressing that Tinubu is pursuing multiple major projects simultaneously. Umahi commended the President for the scale of infrastructure development and economic reforms, citing declining inflation, improved foreign exchange access for businesses and the absence of ASUU strikes. He urged Nigerians, particularly South-East residents in Lagos, to support the President, noting that the administration has delivered significant infrastructure projects to the region. Meanwhile, Umahi has ordered a three-week nationwide emergency rehabilitation of major federal highways ahead of the festive season and the January 2027 elections. He directed Zonal Directors, Controllers, Resident Engineers and contractors to return to the field immediately to ensure critical roads are made motorable across all six geopolitical zones. “I feel so sad that a contractor will be on site doing permanent work, yet some sections of the roads remain impassable. This practice must stop,” he said. He warned that contractors must not allow motorists to suffer on failed sections while permanent construction continues, directing that damaged portions be excavated and rehabilitated using appropriate materials and asphalt where necessary. item.title: Democrats win largest US House majority since 1992
item.description: Democrats have won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives in more than three decades, after Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina, US media projected on Sunday. The party won full control of both the House and Senate in a sweeping midterm rout with a landslide of upsets that delivered a crushing rebuke of President Donald Trump and his Republican Party. CBS News and NBC News projected Hubbard’s win on Sunday, securing the Democrats a 258th seat in Congress’ 435-member House. The majority is the largest won by either party since 1992, when Bill Clinton won the presidency and Democrats won a total of 258 seats. “House Democrats have just secured the largest majority any party in Congress has held this century. BOOM,” House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said in a post on X. Sunday’s result came after Foxx requested a recount. Hubbard said Sunday that he had spoken with Foxx, who “graciously conceded following the results of the recount process.” “Let me be the first to thank Congresswoman Foxx for her decades of service and countless sacrifices,” he added on X. The Democratic victory hands the party the power to block Trump’s agenda and investigate alleged corruption for the last two years of his presidency. The midterm results reflected deep anger over living costs, tariffs and Trump’s war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president. item.title: African players in Europe: Mixed fortunes for Nigerian Awoniyi
item.description: Nigerian Taiwo Awoniyi scored for Coventry City and later had to be substituted after collapsing in a Premier League victory over Crystal Palace at the weekend. AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues: ENGLAND TAIWO AWONIYI (Coventry City) The striker scored his third goal for Coventry in a 3-2 win against bottom club Palace, but his afternoon came to a bizarre premature end. Awoniyi netted in the fifth minute with a close-range finish into the far corner from Jack Rudoni’s pass to put Coventry 1-0 up at the CBS Arena. But the 29-year-old, signed from Nottingham Forest in the close season, was forced to miss the last 45 minutes after going down clutching his leg in pain while the players were lining up to start the second half. Awoniyi had to be helped up off the ground by two Palace players and limped off, forcing bemused Coventry boss Frank Lampard to make an unexpected substitution. Lampard admitted afterwards that Awoniyi felt a slight problem with his ankle from the first half. SPAIN YASSIR ZABIRI (Racing Santander) Moroccan forward Zabiri struck twice in the opening stages to help Santander beat Real Sociedad 3-2 in La Liga. The 21-year-old, on loan from Rennes, climbed to 11 league goals and trails only Raphinha and Kylian Mbappe in the Spanish scoring charts. Zabiri smashed home in the sixth minute for the opener and two minutes later was alert to pinch the ball from Real Sociedad’s goalkeeper and roll it into the empty net for his second. GERMANY JUMA BAH (Augsburg) Sierra Leone and Augsburg centre-back Bah netted his first goal since arriving on a season-long loan from Manchester City in his side’s 3-1 home romp over Mainz in the Bundesliga. With Augsburg 1-0 up, Bah was on the spot to prod a loose ball across the line from a corner to give the hosts their second. FRANCE PATRICK ZABI (Paris FC) Ivorian Zabi opened the scoring just after half-time as second-placed Paris FC hammered lowly visitors Angers 4-0 to lie second in Ligue 1 after 11 rounds, three points behind European champions Paris Saint-Germain. A cross was nodded into the path of the 20-year-old, and he slammed the ball into the net. BOULAYE DIA (Lorient) Dia, a 2022 Africa Cup of Nations champion with Senegal, put Lorient ahead away to Rennes in a 1-1 draw between mid-table clubs. item.title: 2027: Tinubu won’t be included in my national unity govt — Makinde
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Action Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has ruled out including President Bola Tinubu in his proposed government of national unity if elected in 2027, accusing the president of failing to honour an agreement they reached ahead of the 2023 election. Makinde, however, said he would consider appointing capable members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) into his government, insisting that there were decent people in the ruling party who could contribute to governance. He stated this during an interview on The Rooftop Podcast, where he was asked whether he would bring former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi and Tinubu into his government if elected. “Perhaps not President Tinubu, but there are still decent people in APC as well. I’ll tap them and they are Nigerians,” Makinde said. Asked whether he did not consider Tinubu decent, the governor said his position was informed by his experience working with the president during the 2023 election, when an agreement on a government of national unity was allegedly reached but not fulfilled. “Well, not in that context. I mean, I worked for him in 2023. We agreed on a government of national unity. He did not fulfil it,” he said. Makinde explained that the agreement was part of the position taken by the PDP G5 governors, who broke ranks with the party’s leadership ahead of the 2023 presidential election, saying they wanted an inclusive government that would draw competent Nigerians from across the country, irrespective of political affiliation. “We came from the PDP as G5 and we said, ‘Look, this is not going to be a government of APC. It should be a government where you tap people from all across the country. Go to every corner of the country, pick and choose people that can help you know to sort some of this out,’” he said. The APM candidate said the idea of a government of national unity was not new, citing the administration of the late military Head of State, General Sani Abacha, as an example of efforts to bring prominent Nigerians into government to ease political tensions. He recalled that following the annulment of the June 12, 1993 presidential election, Abacha appointed prominent figures, including former Lagos State governor Lateef Jakande and businessman Alex Ibru, to his government. Makinde said the appointments were intended to calm tensions and pacify aggrieved Nigerians. “And it’s been done before. After the annulment of the June 12, 1993 elections, and General Abacha came into government, they went and tapped Alhaji Jakande, Alex Ibru, all of those were geared towards bringing down the temperature in the country and ensuring that where there are angry people, they are being pacified,” he said. item.title: Tourist accuses Daura Emir of sexual assault
item.description: The Emir of Daura, His Royal Highness Alhaji Faruq Umar-Faruk, has been embroiled in an alleged sexual assault of a foreign tourist who visited his palace in Daura, Katsina State, during her tour of Nigeria. The tourist, who identified herself on Instagram as @beduinqa, alleged in a viral video that the 92-year-old monarch fondled her hand and other body parts. The video has elicited reactions, with Amnesty International Nigeria and prominent voices in the North calling for a thorough probe into the act. When contacted, the Daura Emirate spokesperson (Sarkin Labarai), Ibrahim Murtala, confirmed that the Emirate has seen the video and they are currently analyzing its content, adding that the Emirate will address the matter after the conclusion of the ongoing processes. He did not respond to a text message sent to him either. The Katsina State Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), Abubakar Sadiq Aliyu, said the command was not aware of the video and did not receive any formal complaint from anyone on the matter. Describing the alleged experience, the tourist said she found it disgusting and had continued to think about what happened. She explained that although the incident occurred on November 14, she chose not to make it public until she had completed her tour and left the country.
